topics.title: The layoffs say 'AI.' The hiring data says something else.
topics.why: Cuts jumped 199% in September alone (Oracle's 30,000-person round leading the way), while the same week's hiring feed logged zero announced hires — worth separating the AI-blame headline from what's actually driving the freeze.

topics.title: 88% of companies use AI. 79% say it's not working.
topics.why: New enterprise data shows adoption cresting near-universal while most organizations still can't get measurable ROI out of it — a gap that determines whether your employer's AI push helps or hurts your job.

topics.title: Reddit's CEO wants to hire only 'AI-native' new grads. What does that actually mean for you?
topics.why: As IBM triples entry-level AI hiring even while automating HR roles away, 'AI-native' is turning into the resume line that decides who gets the interview — worth defining before it becomes a filter you can't see.

topics.title: AI eval work just split into two tiers — and only one pays $80/hr.
topics.why: The AI training/eval gig market is bifurcating fast: general annotation still sits around $20/hr while domain-expert evaluation is pulling $80+/hr, a concrete near-term option for readers with real subject expertise.

topics.title: 1 billion workers need reskilling. 4% are doing anything about it.
topics.why: WEF's number is huge but the real story is the action gap it hides — most workers feel the anxiety but haven't taken a single concrete step, which is exactly the gap this newsletter's readers are trying to close.
